items.title: Reading the heads
items.prose: To see what each head looks at, write `head_patterns(X, params, h)`, returning the causal attention weights of every head as an array of shape $(h, T, T)$.
items.question: Complete `head_patterns`.

    # the causal attention weights of every head: an array (h, T, T), rows summing to 1
    ...
widget.solution:
import numpy as np


def head_patterns(X, params, h):
    X = np.asarray(X, dtype=float)
    T, d = X.shape
    w = d // h
    Q = (X @ params['Wq']).reshape(T, h, w).transpose(1, 0, 2)
    K = (X @ params['Wk']).reshape(T, h, w).transpose(1, 0, 2)
    S = Q @ K.transpose(0, 2, 1) / np.sqrt(w) + np.triu(np.full((T, T), -np.inf), 1)
    S = S - S.max(axis=-1, keepdims=True)
    A = np.exp(S)
    return A / A.sum(axis=-1, keepdims=True)

items.title: Why the mask comes first
items.prose: Argue that the causal mask must be added to the scores before the softmax, not applied to the weights after it. Put the steps in order and leave out the two that do not belong.
items.question: Order the argument.

lines.text: The softmax divides each $e^{s_{tj}}$ by $\sum_j e^{s_{tj}}$, a sum over every key it is given.
If the future keys are in that sum, their scores change every weight of row $t$, even ones later set to 0.
So zeroing future weights after the softmax still lets future tokens shape the row, and the row no longer sums to 1.
Adding $-\infty$ to the future scores first makes $e^{-\infty} = 0$, so they leave the sum entirely.
Then the softmax spreads a weight of exactly 1 over keys 1 to $t$, and no future token affects output $t$.
Zeroing after the softmax is equivalent, since the zeroed weights multiply future values by 0 anyway.
lines.why: The values are zeroed, but the normaliser already contained the future scores, so every remaining weight depends on them.

lines.text: Masking with $-1$ instead of $-\infty$ removes the future keys just as well.
lines.why: $e^{-1} = 0.37$ is far from 0: the future keys would keep a large share.

feedback.correct: What the normaliser sums over, why that leaks, then why $-\infty$ first fixes it.
feedback.generic: Not quite. Start from what the softmax divides by.

byKey.d1: Zeroing the values does not undo the normaliser, which already saw the future scores.
byKey.d2: Only $-\infty$ gives an exact 0 after the exponential.
byKey.left-out: Every line but the two distractors belongs.

explain.text: The leak lives in the normaliser: any key in the sum shapes every weight of the row. Adding $-\infty$ first removes future keys from the sum, so each row sums to 1 over the past alone.

items.title: A model too good in training
items.prompt: A junior's model of a day's ticks uses self-attention to predict the next price. Its training loss is far better than its out-of-sample loss. Find the likely leak and say how to test for it.
items.model:
**What is wrong.** A training score far better than the out-of-sample score, from attention over a day's ticks, points to a leak: positions are reading the future. Unmasked self-attention lets tick $t$ attend to ticks after it, so a model trained to predict the next price can read the price it is predicting. Training loss collapses; out of sample, with the future absent, it fails.

**Where to look.** (1) A missing or wrong causal mask. It may be absent, added after the softmax (rows stop summing to 1 and the normaliser has seen the future), or have the diagonal or direction wrong. (2) Features built with future data: a day's volume-weighted price or close used at tick $t$, or normalising by the whole day's mean and standard deviation. (3) Targets misaligned by one step.

**How to test.** A leak test: take a sequence, change the ticks after $t$, and assert that outputs 1 to $t$ do not change, for several $t$. Check the attention matrices are lower triangular with rows summing to 1. Rebuild the features with only data known at each tick, and compare training and validation loss on a walk-forward split; the gap should shrink to an honest size.

**Fix.** Add the causal mask to the scores before the softmax, keep the diagonal, and make the leak test part of the build.

rubric.text: Names look-ahead (a leak of future ticks) as the likely cause of the train and test gap
Explains how unmasked attention lets tick $t$ read later ticks, including its own target
Mentions masking after the softmax (or a wrong mask direction or diagonal) as a subtle variant
Mentions leaky features or normalisation using the whole day
Describes a leak test: change later ticks, check earlier outputs are unchanged
Checks the attention matrix is lower triangular with rows summing to 1
Proposes the fix and a walk-forward check of training against validation loss

items.title: Causal multi-head attention with positions
items.prose: Write `causal_mha_forward(X, params, h)`. Add the learned positions `params["P"][:T]` to the embeddings `X` ($T \times d$) and project with `Wq`, `Wk`, `Wv`. Split into $h$ heads of width $d/h$, apply scaled attention with a causal mask in every head, join the heads and multiply by `Wo`. `planted(T, d, seed)` makes test data.
items.question: Complete `causal_mha_forward`.

widget.solution:
import numpy as np


def causal_mha_forward(X, params, h):
    X = np.asarray(X, dtype=float)
    T, d = X.shape
    w = d // h
    x = X + params['P'][:T]
    split = lambda a: a.reshape(T, h, w).transpose(1, 0, 2)
    Q, K, V = split(x @ params['Wq']), split(x @ params['Wk']), split(x @ params['Wv'])
    S = Q @ K.transpose(0, 2, 1) / np.sqrt(w) + np.triu(np.full((T, T), -np.inf), 1)
    S = S - S.max(axis=-1, keepdims=True)
    A = np.exp(S)
    A = A / A.sum(axis=-1, keepdims=True)
    return (A @ V).transpose(1, 0, 2).reshape(T, d) @ params['Wo']
